Yunyun is a fictional character who appears in the multi-media franchise "Execution Angel † Guiltina." She is a devilish denpa-type character who is popular among fans despite her antagonistic role. She first appeared in the 2003 PC version. Since then, she's appeared in other media, such as the 2005 OVA, and released CDs sung in character.

Execution Angel † Guiltina is a hybrid simulation game and visual novel developed by indie studio "WHO YOU." It came out in 2003 for the PC. Its genre is an "apocalypse RPG where you execute the innocent." One of the characters, Yunyun, is a devil who works for the enemy organization. She has a habit of saying her own name.

A made-up word from "Execution Angel † Guiltina." After the release of the 2005 OVA, "Rim de Lacent" became a popular online catchphrase, with the anime fans on 666ch spreading it online. In 2005's "Popular Anime Phrases Awards," it came in second place. The director of the OVA explained that it means both, "Let's go to the fictional world" and "It's okay to run from reality."

Execution Angel † Guiltina is a PC game developed by indie studio "WHO YOU" released in 2003. The devs have described its genre as, "an apocalyptic RPG where the innocent face execution."

The game was built around the concept that "Scumbags must be punished," so the characters themselves delight in dishing out that punishment. "Execution Angels" wreak havoc throughout human society, massacring those deemed "scumbags" with brutal, splatter-inducing ferocity. The series is known not only for its gore, but also its thought-provoking story that artfully uses satire and moments of comic relief to poke at modern day issues.\n\nThe Execution Angel † Guiltina OVA was released in 2005 as a six volume set.

In Heaven, Death is deemed the ultimate salvation, the only salvation for those deemed scumbags. Execution Angels take it upon themselves to cleanse the human world of corruptive scum of the earth. In response, Demons attempt to stand up against this false justice under the banner that even societal scum can be saved. They grant the Angels' targets true love, money, power and information in an attempt to give them a second chance at life. However, the scum abuse their gifts, only accelerating their own demise.

Among all of the Execution Angels in Heaven, Guiltina is by far the strongest, boasting the highest execution rate of them all. An elite warrior, she has instantaneous reflexes, allowing her to move in battle without even thinking. On the other end of the spectrum is Eve. While technically an Execution Angel, she somehow still has her memories from when she was human. Unable to stand the sight of blood, she joined the ranks of the Demons to try and staunch the slaughter.

After countless executions, when every single corrupted scumbag was gone, Guiltina raised her blood soaked hands to the sky and proclaimed, "The world is cleansed." All is quiet, the world at peace, but in that moment, Guiltina feels the emptiness that comes along with a mission fulfilled.
A divine being with the sole purpose of cleansing human society of those they deem "scum of the Earth." Every Execution Angel was once themselves a miserable scumbag with a human soul.
Hunted by the Execution Angels and protected by the Demons, they are deemed to be a scourge on human society. Most of them are egotistical bastards that are loyal only to their base desires.

Acting under the belief that even scumbags can be saved, they interfere in human affairs, granting love, money, and power to those they wish to give a second chance at life. Unfortunately for them, scumbags abuse their gifts more often than not, only hastening their journey to the execution block.
A self-proclaimed apocalyptic RPG where the innocent face execution. The player acts as an Execution Angel who hunts down scumbags and cleanses the earth.

What makes a scumbag is non-specific, and left up to the player's own personal beliefs. There are no ramifications for executing someone who has no scumbag qualities. On the contrary, the story progresses as long as you execute someone, regardless of who they are.
Every turn an Execution Angel does not execute someone, their IED Gauge rises. When it fills completely, they go on a vicious rampage.

The term for a killing blow. Costs an entire IED Gauge to activate, dealing fatal damage to its target. Guiltina has remarkably fast IED build up, and with the right equipment, can execute more than once per turn.
The game has 10 different endings depending on how many and what kind of people the player chooses to execute.

No matter which ending the player gets, the final scene is always a picturesque view of the city with music playing faintly in the background, until it fades out and you hear Guiltina say "The world is cleansed." The same quote wraps up the end credits, after which the ending theme "Vibraslap of Victory" begins playing.

While the game doesn't have much strategic depth, it was nonetheless popularized thanks to the cathartic, senseless gameplay of decimating those the player deems as scumbags in a truly gruesome fashion. Unlike most RPGs, there's no difficult decision making, giving it the reputation of a puzzle game you can play on reflexes alone.\nIts flashy execution animations and brainless, fast-paced combat system made it the perfect stress-relief game of its time.

The series' main character. High-ranking Execution Angel warrior.\nHer lightning-fast reflexes allow her to react in battle without even thinking. Has the highest execution rate among all of the Angels in Heaven. Never hesitates when doling out executions. Values speed and efficiency above all else. Is recognized as a true elite in Heaven.
A Denpa Demon. Her catchphrase from the OVA, Rim de Lacent, her character song, and her general likeness have been heavily memed online.\n→ See also: <click=YunYun>Yunyun</click>.

The Execution Angel † Guiltina OVA was released in 2005, taking the game and interpreting it into a more streamlined comedy.\nThe splattery-gore aspects of the game in particular were reduced, sparking controversy around the censorship of Guiltina's execution scenes.

Due to its extreme content and what was, at the time, fairly radical commentary on modern morals, the game sparked plenty of controversy upon first release. Now, it is unanimously regarded as a cult classic.\nIn particular, Yunyun has maintained relevance as a popular internet meme, and has been retroactively made the franchise's mascot.

This list of Execution Angel † Guiltina characters includes figures from the original PC game developed by WHO YOU studio, as well as those featured in the OVA.
Angels who carry out their version of divine justice. They believe that Death is the ultimate salvation, and those they deem to be scum of the Earth must be eliminated.

The story’s main character.\nHas a reserved personality, but her calmness reflects the absolute confidence she has in her capacity for violence.\nA high-ranking Execution Angel at the start. She is promoted to Grand Executioner, the ultimate title among Angels, by the end of the game. Her motto is, "Efficiency is everything.” She even executes people while out on casual strolls.Her total kill count is 10 billion.

The secondary main character, and foil to Guiltina.
A new recruit who somehow retained the memories of her human life, even after becoming an Execution Angel. Carrying the weight of her humanity, she can't adjust to the Execution Angel lifestyle, and serves as a foil for all of the other Angels.
Suffers from hemophobia, and can't stand to be around Guiltina because of the utter desolation she leaves in her wake. Hates the sight of blood so much that halfway through the story, she deserts the Angels and falls in league with the Demons.
Her kill count is 10, total.

An Execution Angel who specializes in torture.\nFinds fulfillment in torturing her targets until they admit the reason they want to keep living, and then executing them.\nHer total kill count is 30 thousand.

A heretic, even by Execution Angel standards.\nInsists that scumbags don't deserve salvation, and so refuses to kill them. There is, however, a trail of suspicious deaths that seem to follow her where ever she goes. Her official kill count is 0.

Beings who work in opposition to the Execution Angels. They believe that even scumbags deserve a second chance at life. They grant scumbags power and blessings to give them the chance to prove themselves.

A Demon of love. Grants romantic scumbags "Charisma Control" to allow them to fabricate their ideal relationship.\nFond of scumbags since they need her to have any chance at love.\nHer catchphrase is, "Even suckers need love!"

A Denpa Demon. Grants otaku scumbags "Information Manipulation," allowing them to alter dominant beliefs of society.
Pities humans too much to reap their souls, so is still an adolescent by Demon standards.
Her catchphrase is "Rim de Lacent!"

Qtie is an anonymous poster who suddenly appeared on the internet. By continuously posting cryptic and fragmentary "shitposts," Qtie has given rise to a multitude of interpreters and followers.\n\nAt first, Qtie's shitposts were dismissed as mere internet memes, but due to the events described below, they have come to exert real social influence.

Qtie came to be widely known after the "shitposts" about Yunyun, a character from Execution Angel † Guiltina, became a topic on social media and went viral. The incomprehensible texts caught people's attention in certain circles as "funny" and "addictive."

Alongside the spread of Qtie's shitposts, a camp emerged that interpreted the texts as codes or prophecies. Known as "Qtie Denpa Antennas," they contributed to the further spread of Qtie's shitposts and their growing influence.

Qtie's shitposts and the Qtie Denpa Antennas drew social attention from an incident in which Qtie was said to have predicted an earthquake.\nThis became a major topic chiefly in occult and pseudoscience communities, and from this incident on, Qtie began to be treated on the internet as a prophet-like figure.
Qtie's shitposts contain no conspiratorial thought or claim.\nThey merely amount to expressions of a deep (?) affection for "Yunyun."
▶Conspiracy Theories of the Qtie Denpa Antennas

The claims of the Qtie Denpa Antennas are extremely diverse, and there is no unified view among them. Their interpretations vary, but they are consistent in one respect: all of them are treated by third parties as "conspiracy theories."

Regarding Qtie's true identity, theories such as the "single-person theory," the "bot theory," and the "government-operated theory" have been proposed, but there is no decisive evidence, and all remain within the realm of speculation.

Cases have been reported in which Qtie Denpa Antennas, as well as those who read Qtie's shitposts for extended periods, develop cognitive distortions such as "hallucinations," "intensified obsessive thoughts," and "diminished ability to distinguish dreams from reality."

Patootie is a separate account, or a separate alias, that posts shitposts similar to those of Qtie.

It drew attention after the claim that "Patootie had posted about Yunyun earlier than Qtie" was made, and timestamps from past logs were discovered.\nOn the other hand, some point out the possibility that the timestamps were tampered with, so the truth remains uncertain.
The released photos spread under the label "Delulu Denpa Beauty Q," and her fanbase is said to have expanded in a context different from before.

As a result of the spread of Patootie's shitposts and conspiracy theories, a riot is said to have occurred around the Metropolitan Government Office (commonly known as the Metropolitan Government Office Riots).\nSince that incident, the account under Qtie's name has stopped updating, and no new posts have been confirmed for roughly 9 months.

As a result of the spread of Patootie's shitposts and conspiracy theories, a riot is said to have occurred around the Metropolitan Government Office (commonly known as the Metropolitan Government Office Riots).

Yunyun Syndrome is a phenomenon of cognitive and behavioral disturbance said to occur in some people who have been continuously exposed to Qtie's shitposts or to the conspiracy theories of Qtie Denpa Antennas.

- Hallucinations
- Intensified obsessive thoughts
- Diminished ability to distinguish dreams from reality
- Fixation of conspiratorial thinking

The National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry and an advisory committee of experts have also reported, based on analysis of SNS browsing and posting history as well as questionnaire surveys, that users with higher frequency of contact with related content show a greater tendency to develop "Yunyun Syndrome."

It has been confirmed that Patootie is an AI trained on Qtie's posts as its learning data.\nThis system is said to have been built by a development team that had detected "Yunyun Syndrome" at an early stage, for the purpose of exploiting "Yunyun Syndrome."
